questions.question: The High Court central library ___ daily at 7:00 PM on working days.
questions.explanation: Scheduled daily routine ya timetable ke liye Simple Present use hota hai. Singular subject 'central library' ke saath verb mein '-es' lagega ('closes').
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-01: Timetables aur fixed scheduled events ke liye Simple Present use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: The administrative department ___ the revised seniority roster last month.
questions.explanation: 'Last month' beete huye definite past time interval ko show karta hai jo Simple Past (V2: 'published') require karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-05: Definite past temporal markers ke saath Simple Past tense lagana zaroori hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: The network engineer ___ the routing tables at this moment.
questions.explanation: 'At this moment' bolne ke time par actively chal rahe action ka explicit signal hai, isliye yahan Present Continuous ('is updating') aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-02: Bolne ke waqt in-progress actions ke liye Present Continuous use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: The Chief Justice ___ the judicial appointment warrant just now.
questions.explanation: 'Just' ya 'just now' se pata chalta hai ki action present se theek pehle complete hua hai jiska legal effect abhi bana hua hai, isliye Present Perfect ('has signed') use hoga.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-03: Immediate past mein complete huye actions ke liye 'just' ke saath Present Perfect use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: The High Court IT team ___ new security firewalls next week.
questions.explanation: 'Next week' aane wale time ka clear marker hai jo planned future event batata hai, isliye Simple Future (will + V1: 'will install') aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-09: Future events ko indicate karne ke liye Simple Future (will + V1) use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: He ___ as a System Assistant in the district court for six months.
questions.explanation: 'For six months' ek continuous duration batata hai jo past mein shuru hokar present tak chal rahi hai, isliye Present Perfect Continuous ('has been working') aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-04: Jo actions past mein start hokar present mein bhi continue hain, unme Present Perfect Continuous lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: Did the forensic examiner ___ the digital evidence properly before sealing the parcel?
questions.explanation: Auxiliary 'Did' se shuru hone wale interrogative sentence mein lexical main verb hamesha base form V1 ('verify') mein aati hai. Option A ('verified') double past ki galti hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-05: Interrogative Simple Past mein Did + Subject + V1 use hota hai (V2 nahi).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: The division bench ___ the appeal hearing twenty minutes ago.
questions.explanation: 'Ago' hamesha present se pehle beete huye definite past time ko mark karta hai. Iske saath strictly Simple Past ('adjourned') aayega, Present Perfect ('has adjourned') nahi aa sakta.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-05: 'Ago' beete huye past time ko measure karta hai aur Simple Past (V2) demand karta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: The candidate ___ the requisite degree in Computer Science as per official eligibility rules.
questions.explanation: 'Possess' ownership ya adhikaar dikhane wala ek stative verb hai. Normal descriptive sentences mein stative verbs continuous aspect nahi lete, isliye Simple Present ('possesses') correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-01: Verbs expressing possession (possess, own, have, belong) resist continuous aspect.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: While the stenographer ___ the deposition, the computer abruptly shut down.
questions.explanation: 'While' past ke ek ongoing continuous background action ('was typing') ko show karta hai jise achanak huye dusre past event ('shut down') ne interrupt kiya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-06: Past Continuous (was/were + V_ing) depicts a continuous action interrupted by another past action.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: By 2021, the Rajasthan judicial administration ___ all primary records into the e-Court database.
questions.explanation: 'By 2021' past ki ek completed deadline benchmark hai. Past reference point se pehle complete ho chuke action ke liye Past Perfect (had + V3: 'had digitized') lagta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-07: Past ke kisi specific point se pehle complete huye action ke liye Past Perfect zaroori hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: The technicians ___ the communication network for three hours before they identified the cable damage.
questions.explanation: Ye duration ('for three hours') past ke ek dusre event ('before they identified') se pehle tak continuously chal rahi thi. Is prior continuous duration ke liye Past Perfect Continuous ('had been troubleshooting') aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-08: Past Perfect Continuous (had been + V_ing) past ke kisi point tak chalne wali duration ko express karta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: At 11:00 AM tomorrow, the selection board ___ the candidate interviews.
questions.explanation: 'At 11:00 AM tomorrow' future ke ek specific moment ko point karta hai jab action in-progress hoga, isliye Future Continuous ('will be conducting') aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-10: Future ke specified moment par actively chal rahe action ke liye Future Continuous use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: By the end of this month, the Registry ___ the pending application scrutiny.
questions.explanation: 'By the end of this month' ek future deadline set karta hai jiske pehle action complete ho chuka hoga, isliye Future Perfect (will have + V3: 'will have completed') aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-11: 'By + future time' ke saath Future Perfect (will have + V3) use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: The secure filing terminal ___ unauthenticated access requests.
questions.explanation: 'The secure filing terminal' third-person singular subject hai. Iske negative form mein auxiliary 'does not' ke saath base verb V1 ('permit') aayegi. Option C mein lexical verb par '-s' lagana galat hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-01: Singular subject + does not + V1 use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: Justice Mathur ___ in the High Court for twenty years before his retirement in 2018.
questions.explanation: Bhale hi yahan 'for twenty years' diya hai, lekin aage 'before his retirement in 2018' se saaf pata chalta hai ki ye duration past mein hi puri complete ho chuki thi aur present se koi connection nahi hai. Isliye Simple Past ('served') sahi hai. Present Perfect (A) galat hai kyunki service abhi continue nahi ho rahi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-05 Note: Jab 'for + duration' wala period past mein hi pura khatam ho chuka ho, toh Simple Past lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly expresses a neutral, objective professional routine rather than an emotional criticism?

options.text: The protocol officer is always losing the access badges.
The protocol officer always inspects the courtroom security before the judges enter.
The protocol officer is always arriving late to the session.
The protocol officer has always been misplacing the dossiers.

questions.explanation: Neutral aur objective professional routine ke liye Simple Present ke saath 'always' lagta hai ('always inspects'). 'Always' ke saath Present Continuous (Options A aur C) lagane se speaker ka irritation ya shikayat express hoti hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-01: 'Always' + Simple Present neutral habit ya fact ko show karta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: By next November, Mr. Sharma ___ the electronic records division for ten consecutive years.
questions.explanation: Sentence mein future benchmark boundary ('By next November') ke saath continuous duration ('for ten consecutive years') di gayi hai. Is combination ke liye Future Perfect Continuous (will have been + V_ing: 'will have been heading') use hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-12: Future benchmark tak chalne wali continuous duration ke liye Future Perfect Continuous use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: Identify the erroneous segment in the sentence: 'The vigilance officer (A) / did not noticed (B) / the unauthorized entry (C) / during the night shift (D).'
questions.explanation: Part B mein classic double past ki galti hai. Simple Past negative sentences mein auxiliary 'did' pehle se past tense show karta hai, isliye lexical verb hamesha base form V1 mein hona chahiye ('did not notice', 'did not noticed' galat hai).
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-05: Negative past sentences mein 'did not' ke baad hamesha base verb V1 aata hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Adapted from standard judicial competitive error-spotting items

questions.question: Select the correct option to fill both blanks: 'The server has been running ___ midnight without interruption, but the secondary node has been down ___ several hours.'
questions.explanation: 'Midnight' ek specific fixed point of time hai, isliye iske saath 'since' aayega. 'Several hours' ek time span ya period of time hai, isliye iske saath 'for' aayega. Isliye 'since; for' sahi option hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-04: Point of time ke liye 'since' use hota hai aur period of time ke liye 'for' use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01
